items.q: Le Fort III fracture is defined by what separation?
o: Craniofacial disjunction: entire facial skeleton separated from skull base
items.exp: Le Fort III runs through zygomatic arches, lateral orbits and nasal bridge separating face from cranium (floating face) with highest CSF and airway risk. I separates palate, II pyramids midface.
r: Incorrect. Palate level is Le Fort I.
Correct. Whole face disjoined in III.
Incorrect. Mandible is lower face separate system.
Incorrect. Nasal only is isolated nasal fracture.

items.q: Child with eye trauma, minimal bruising, cannot elevate eye, nausea and bradycardia needs what?
o: Urgent orbital CT and surgical release of trapdoor blowout with entrapped muscle
items.exp: White eyed blowout: elastic child bone trapdoors inferior rectus causing oculocardiac reflex; delay necroses muscle and fixes diplopia, so urgent ophthalmic maxillofacial surgery.
r: Incorrect. Weeks delay causes permanent restriction.
items.kp: Quiet white eye that cannot look up operates tonight.

items.q: Clear watery unilateral nasal discharge after frontal trauma, salty taste, is confirmed as CSF by which test?
items.exp: Beta 2 transferrin is CSF specific (also perilymph) and reliable; glucose strips false positive from tears and mucus and are obsolete for this use. Collect fluid without contaminating blood where possible.
r: Incorrect. Culture grows contaminants, not origin.

items.q: Proptosis, tense rock hard globe, severe pain and falling vision after facial trauma demand what before imaging?
o: Immediate lateral canthotomy and cantholysis for orbital compartment syndrome from retrobulbar haemorrhage
items.exp: Retrobulbar bleed raises intraorbital pressure strangling optic nerve and retina; bedside canthotomy releases orbit within minutes and cannot await scans when clinical syndrome is present.
items.kp: Tight blind eye: release orbit at bedside.

items.q: Most traumatic CSF rhinorrhoea management in first week is what?
o: Conservative: head up, avoid straining, sneezing suppression, no nose blowing; surgery if persistent or meningitis
Lumbar drain for all day one
items.exp: Majority seal spontaneously within seven to ten days with elevation and pressure precautions; antibiotics do not prevent meningitis and select resistance. Persistent leaks, pneumocephalus or meningitis go endoscopic repair pathways.
r: Correct. Conservative first week, repair if persists.
Incorrect. Drains are selective specialist tools.
items.kp: Sit up, do not strain, most leaks seal.

items.q: Bilateral parasymphyseal mandibular fractures threaten airway chiefly because what?
o: Anterior mandible flail loses tongue support, tongue falls back obstructing
items.exp: Glossoptosis from detached genial muscle support obstructs supine airway; positioning, suction, jaw support and definitive airway planning precede fixation. Ring principle also mandates searching second fracture.
r: Correct. Tongue falls back from flail segment.
Incorrect. Spine checked but separate mechanism.
items.kp: Broken jaw both sides drops the tongue.

items.q: Cheek flattening, infraorbital numbness, trismus and diplopia after punch indicate which fracture?
o: Zygomatic complex (tripod) fracture with orbital floor involvement
items.exp: Tetrapod zygoma fractures displace at frontozygomatic, infraorbital, zygomaticomaxillary and arch points causing this sign cluster; CT guides reduction (Gillies approach patterns) and floor repair indications.
r: Incorrect. Le Fort I floats palate.
Incorrect. Frontal alone lacks cheek pattern.
items.kp: Flat numb cheek that cannot open: zygoma.

items.q: In midface fracture repair, the functional priority restored first is what?
o: Dental occlusion (then facial buttresses and height)
items.exp: Maxillomandibular fixation re establishes premorbid occlusion as foundation; buttress plating then restores vertical and projection dimensions. Cosmetic sequencing follows function.
r: Incorrect. Airway matters but bite anchors repair.

items.q: Reservoir sign in CSF rhinorrhoea refers to what?
o: Gush of clear fluid on leaning forward after pooling in sinus
items.exp: CSF collects in frontal or sphenoid sinus while upright or supine then drains in gush on bending (reservoir or teapot sign), classic history separating from continuous rhinitis drip.
r: Incorrect. Scan pooling is separate finding.
Correct. Bending releases pooled CSF gush.
items.kp: Lean forward, clear gush: pooled CSF.

items.q: Entrapped inferior rectus in blowout causes diplopia worst in which gaze and why?
o: Upgaze; tethered inferior rectus cannot relax and globe cannot elevate
All gazes equally from swelling only
items.exp: Floor fracture traps or tethers inferior rectus so elevation fails and diplopia peaks looking up, with forced duction restriction confirming mechanical cause over nerve palsy.
r: Correct. Upgaze fails from tethered inferior muscle.
Incorrect. Medial wall traps medial rectus horizontally.
Incorrect. Swelling diplopia differs and forced duction free.
items.kp: Cannot look up because muscle below is caught.
